calibration.use: Monte Carlo around it, or an imported drag table scaled by it; if the motor under-performed, thrust is the more likely cause (compare time to apogee and the boost phase)

accelerometer.coastDrag: 0.8073 x OpenRocket's (drag / mass / v^2, 0.3 to 1.07 s after burnout)
accelerometer.thrustFactor: 0.9096 x the motor's thrust gives the measured burnout velocity
accelerometer.dragFactor: 0.7578 x OpenRocket's drag then gives the measured apogee (the coast measured 0.8073)
accelerometer.apogeeDifference: -114.1 m (-374.5 ft) in all: -196.7 m (-645.5 ft) from the boost (thrust x0.9096) and 82.59 m (271 ft) from drag
accelerometer.reading: Mostly the boost: the motor delivered less (or more) than its thrust curve; calibrate drag only after allowing for it.
accelerometer.caveats: Assumes a near-vertical boost and an accelerometer whose gain is right (its offset is removed from the pad reading); motors of one type vary by a few percent in impulse.

notes: Match the simulation to the day: wind, launch angle, site altitude and temperature (run with overrides), and the as-flown mass (edit or override masses) before reading the drag factor.

Barometric altimeters read low near Mach 1 and lag at apogee; the drogue and main bands are fitted slopes, time to apogee counts from lift-off (the log's 10 m crossing less the simulated time to climb 10 m) to the top of a parabola through the samples around apogee.
